game: Kent State Golden Flashes@Ohio State Buckeyes

guide_enrichment.narrative: Our model’s slight lean toward Ohio State starts with the offense’s ability to create scoring opportunities against a Kent State defense that has struggled to prevent them. We see a stable foundation around Julian Sayin, who completed 77.0 percent of his passes last season, and an offensive line that entered 2026 with the highest continuity rate in the Power Four. The opener offered supporting context rather than proof: Ohio State produced 671 yards and spread receptions among 14 players.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
For us, the matchup to watch is Kent State’s rushing offense against Ohio State’s rush defense. Kent State’s rushing efficiency profile is among the weakest in the country, while Ohio State grades near the top defensively. If Kent State cannot stay ahead of schedule on the ground, sustaining possessions and limiting Ohio State’s opportunities becomes much harder.

We still account for uncertainty because Ohio State replaced eight defensive starters from last season. The opening performance—only 45 rushing yards allowed—was encouraging, but one game does not erase that turnover. That tension helps explain why we can favor Ohio State’s matchup without finding enough separation from the market to justify a wager.

recent_game.fact: Ohio State opened the 2026 season with a 56-3 home win over Ball State on Sept. 5.
Against Ball State, Ohio State recorded 671 total yards, including 434 passing and 237 rushing, while allowing 165 total yards, including 45 rushing.
Jeremiah Smith caught eight passes for 151 yards and two touchdowns in the first half of the opener.
Ohio State had 14 players record a reception against Ball State, its first game with at least 14 receivers since Sept. 22, 2018 against Tulane.
Bo Jackson averaged 9.2 yards per carry in the opener and scored on a career-long 65-yard run.
Freshman Legend Bey produced 100 all-purpose yards against Ball State and scored on his first career reception.

quarterback.fact: Julian Sayin is Ohio State's returning starting quarterback and had 15 career starts through the season opener.
Sayin completed 77.0 percent of his passes in 2025, throwing for 3,610 yards, 32 touchdowns and eight interceptions.
Sayin's 77.0 percent completion rate in 2025 set Ohio State and Big Ten single-season records.
Backup quarterback Justyn Martin had appeared in six career games without a start.

offensive_personnel.fact: Ohio State returned eight offensive starters: QB Julian Sayin, RB Bo Jackson, WR Jeremiah Smith, WR Brandon Inniss, OT Phillip Daniels, C Carson Hinzman, OG Luke Montgomery and OG Austin Siereveld.
Ohio State lost starting guard Tegra Tshabola and starting tight ends Max Klare and Will Kacmarek from the 2025 team.
Ohio State entered 2026 with 85.8 percent offensive-line continuity among players who logged at least 100 snaps in 2025, the highest rate in the Power Four.
After the opener, Ohio State's starting offensive line had combined for 146 games played and 93 starts.
The experienced offensive-line returnees included Carson Hinzman with 36 career starts, Austin Siereveld with 21, Phillip Daniels with 17 and Luke Montgomery with 17.
Wide receivers Devin McCuin, Kyle Parker and Brandon Inniss entered the season with 28, seven and seven career starts, respectively; McCuin transferred from UTSA and Parker transferred from LSU.
Tight ends Mason Williams and Hunter Welcing arrived with 26 and 11 career starts, respectively, from Ohio and Northwestern.
Bo Jackson led Ohio State with 1,090 rushing yards on 179 carries in 2025.
Jeremiah Smith entered the Texas week with 171 career receptions, 2,709 receiving yards and 29 receiving touchdowns.

defensive_personnel.fact: Ohio State returned three defensive starters from 2025: cornerback Jermaine Mathews Jr., defensive end Kenyatta Jackson Jr. and safety Jaylen McClain.

The defense lost eight starters: defensive tackles Tywone Malone Jr. and Kayden McDonald, defensive end Caden Curry, linebackers Arvell Reese and Sonny Styles, safeties Caleb Downs and Lorenzo Styles, and cornerback Devin Igbinosun.

Ohio State added experienced defensive transfers James Smith and Qua Russaw from Alabama, John Walker from UCF, Christian Alliegro from Wisconsin, Earl Little Jr. from Florida State and Beau Atkinson from North Carolina.
Safety Earl Little Jr. led Florida State with 76 tackles in 2025 before transferring to Ohio State.
Christian Alliegro entered 2026 with 127 career tackles and eight sacks, including 12 starts at Wisconsin.
Returning safety Jaylen McClain made 15 career starts and logged 816 defensive snaps with 53 tackles in 2025.

coaching_changes.fact: Ohio State's 2026 coordinators are Arthur Smith on offense, Matt Patricia on defense and Robby Discher on special teams.
Tyler Bowen is Ohio State's run game coordinator and offensive line coach, while Billy Fessler is the pass game coordinator and quarterbacks coach.
Cortez Hankton coaches wide receivers, Carlos Locklyn coaches running backs and Keenan Bailey serves as co-offensive coordinator and tight ends coach.

offensive_context.fact: Through the opener, Ohio State averaged 56.0 points and 671 total yards per game, with 434 passing yards and 237 rushing yards.
Ohio State converted 45.5 percent of its third downs and scored on every red-zone opportunity in the opener.
Ohio State is one of two FBS programs, along with Miami, to have produced a 3,500-yard passer, a 1,000-yard receiver and a 1,000-yard rusher in each of the previous two seasons.

defensive_context.fact: Ohio State allowed three points and 165 total yards in the season opener, including 120 passing yards and 45 rushing yards.
Ball State converted 21.4 percent of its third downs and did not score on a red-zone possession against Ohio State.
Ohio State led the FBS in 2025 in scoring defense at 9.3 points allowed per game, total defense at 219.1 yards and passing defense at 129.7 yards.
Since the start of the 2024 season, Ohio State had allowed 37 touchdowns in 31 games and had nine games without allowing a touchdown.

special_teams.fact: Punter Joe McGuire is Ohio State's returning starting specialist.
Ohio State lost starting kicker Jayden Fielding and long snapper John Ferlmann from the 2025 team.
Connor Hawkins and Dalton Riggs are listed as Ohio State's 2026 kicker and long snapper, respectively.

other_relevant.fact: Ohio State is scheduled to host Kent State at noon on Sept. 19, 2026, with FOX carrying the game.
Ohio State entered the season with 34 returning letterwinners and 31 lost letterwinners.
Ohio State played 21 true freshmen in its season-opening win over Ball State.
